sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Sting (1973)
supports: Paul Newman is credited as Henry Gondorff and Robert Redford as Johnny Hooker.
AFI’s synopsis says Hooker goes to Chicago to meet Gondorff for a ‘big con.’
Marvin Hamlisch adapted the score from Scott Joplin melodies; AFI identifies the main theme as based on Joplin’s 1902 ‘The Entertainer.’
sources.limits: Gondorff and the con are fictional. The source supports story and music context, not real-world fraud methods.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 46th Academy Awards (1974)
supports: The Sting received ten nominations and seven wins.
It won Best Picture, Directing for George Roy Hill, Costume Design for Edith Head, Adaptation Score for Marvin Hamlisch, and the original-story-and-screenplay award for David S. Ward.
The ledger also lists cinematography and sound nominations for the film.
sources.limits: The ceremony was held in 1974 for 1973 releases; the ledger supports award outcomes and categories, not plot claims beyond the film identity.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Conversation (1974)
supports: Gene Hackman is credited as Harry Caul; Francis Ford Coppola is credited as director, writer, and producer.
AFI records that Coppola began the screenplay in 1966 and finished it in 1970.
AFI’s fictional plot synopsis places Caul and colleagues recording a conversation in San Francisco’s Union Square.
sources.limits: Harry Caul and the surveillance plot are fictional. The source must not be used as technical guidance or evidence about real surveillance practice.

sources.title: The Conversation — Festival de Cannes
supports: The festival lists The Conversation as a 1974 In Competition feature and records Grand Prix International du Festival 1974.
It credits Francis Ford Coppola for direction and screenplay, Bill Butler for cinematography, and David Shire for music.
Gene Hackman appears in the official cast list.
sources.limits: Use the festival’s historical award name exactly. Do not relabel it as the modern runner-up Grand Prix or claim a different trophy without a separately verified historical source.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 47th Academy Awards (1975)
supports: Its Best Picture nomination names Francis Ford Coppola and Fred Roos.
The other nominations are Sound for Walter Murch and Arthur Rochester and Original Screenplay for Francis Ford Coppola.
sources.limits: The 1975 ceremony ledger supports its listed nominations only; it does not establish facts about the fictional surveillance narrative.
